editorial:
The Dawn Rider is a John Wayne B-western from 1935, directed and written by Robert N. Bradbury. Wikipedia gives a June 20, 1935 release by Monogram Pictures, and its infobox lists the production company as Lone Star Pictures. That is a film credit, not a confirmed copyright claimant. Wayne plays John Mason. Marion Burns plays Alice Gordon, and Reed Howes plays Ben McClure. Yakima Canutt and Earl Dwire are also in the cast. Creators looking for Wayne-era western footage have two Internet Archive uploads to start from.

The print status is undetermined. No renewal was found in the searched OCR text of the 1962, 1963 and 1964 Catalog of Copyright Entries motion-picture volumes, but that search has limits and is not proof of non-renewal. The original 1935 registration entry was not located, so the claimant and title as registered are unconfirmed. The Copyright Office public records were not searched. The open layers are the recorded music, which was not confirmed, and the underlying story, which Wikipedia credits to Lloyd Nosler without a verified source. Trademark and restoration status were not checked. Wayne's name and likeness are a separate matter from the film's copyright, and using them in promotion can raise right-of-publicity issues.
faq: Can I reuse footage from The Dawn Rider?

The copyright status of the film print is not settled. No renewal was found in the searched OCR text of the 1962-1964 Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes, but the original 1935 registration was not located and the Copyright Office records were not searched. Music and story rights were not independently cleared. Do your own check before reusing the footage, soundtrack or plot.
Does John Wayne's appearance create a problem?
Copyright and publicity rights are separate. Footage of the film is one thing. Using Wayne's name or image to endorse or sell something is another, and state right-of-publicity law can apply to that.
